Paris is one of the few world capitals that has rarely seen destruction by catastrophe or war. As a result, even its earliest history is visible in its street map, and centuries of rulers adding their respective architectural marks on the capital have resulted in an accumulated wealth of history-rich monuments and buildings whose beauty plays a large part in giving Paris the reputation it has today.[[132]](#cite_note-134) At its origin, before the Middle Ages, Paris was composed of several islands and sandbanks in a bend of the [Seine](/wiki/Seine "Seine"). fanoutqa_000034.x:
Corey Patterson :: Professional career :: Cincinnati Reds :: chunk_0004
On March 3, 2008, the [Cincinnati Reds](/wiki/Cincinnati_Reds "Cincinnati Reds") signed Patterson to a minor league contract. At the end of Spring training, he was added to the [40-man roster](/wiki/40-man_roster "40-man roster").[[12]](#cite_note-usatoday-12) [Dusty Baker](/wiki/Dusty_Baker "Dusty Baker"), [manager](/wiki/Manager_(baseball) "Manager (baseball)") of the Reds and Patterson's manager in Chicago, was instrumental in signing Patterson.[[12]](#cite_note-usatoday-12) Baker often voiced his opinion on Patterson saying he thought Patterson is still a developing player.[[13]](#cite_note-13)

Patterson was invited to the Reds' spring training camp, and he started the 2008 season in center field for Cincinnati. Platooning with utility man [Ryan Freel](/wiki/Ryan_Freel "Ryan Freel"),[[14]](#cite_note-:4-14) Patterson began the season well. Gradually his average deteriorated, culminating in an 0-for-8 performance during Cincinnati's 18-inning loss to San Diego on May 25.[[15]](#cite_note-:5-15) The following day top outfield prospect Jay Bruce was called up from the Triple-A [Louisville Bats](/wiki/Louisville_Bats "Louisville Bats") to start in center field, demoting Patterson to the Reds' bench. On May 28, Patterson accepted a reassignment to Triple-A Louisville.[[16]](#cite_note-16) The demotion lasted only one week, however, when Patterson was recalled to replace Freel, who went to the disabled list with a strained right hamstring on June 4.[[17]](#cite_note-17)[[14]](#cite_note-:4-14) Patterson ended the season with a .205 batting average and .238 OBP.[[15]](#cite_note-:5-15)

On January 22, 2006, Bryant scored a career-high [81 points](/wiki/Kobe_Bryant%27s_81-point_game "Kobe Bryant's 81-point game"), the third [most scored in a single NBA game](/wiki/List_of_NBA_single-game_scoring_leaders "List of NBA single-game scoring leaders") behind [Wilt Chamberlain's 100-point game](/wiki/Wilt_Chamberlain%27s_100-point_game "Wilt Chamberlain's 100-point game") and [Bam Adebayo's 83-point game](/wiki/Bam_Adebayo%27s_83-point_game "Bam Adebayo's 83-point game"). Bryant led the team to championships in [2009](/wiki/2009_NBA_Finals "2009 NBA Finals") and [2010](/wiki/2010_NBA_Finals "2010 NBA Finals"), and was named NBA Finals MVP both times. He continued to be among the league's premier players through the [2012–13 season](/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_NBA_season "2012–13 NBA season") when he suffered a [torn achilles tendon](/wiki/Torn_achilles_tendon "Torn achilles tendon"). The last years of his playing career were hampered by injuries and limited playing time. Bryant retired after the [2015–16 season](/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_NBA_season "2015–16 NBA season"). In 2017, the Lakers retired both his Nos. 8 and 24, making Bryant the only player in NBA history to have multiple [numbers retired](/wiki/Retired_number "Retired number") by the same franchise.

The all-time leading scorer in Lakers history, Bryant was the first [guard](/wiki/Guard_(basketball) "Guard (basketball)") in NBA history to [play 20 seasons](/wiki/List_of_National_Basketball_Association_seasons_played_leaders "List of National Basketball Association seasons played leaders"). fanoutqa_026658.x:
Cuban Missile Crisis :: Aftermath :: US leadership :: chunk_0041
The worldwide [DEFCON](/wiki/DEFCON "DEFCON") 3 status of US Forces was returned to DEFCON 4 on 20 November 1962. General [Curtis LeMay](/wiki/Curtis_LeMay "Curtis LeMay") told Kennedy that the resolution of the crisis was the "greatest defeat in our history".[[84]](#cite_note-axelrod2009-84) LeMay had pressed for an immediate invasion of Cuba as soon as the crisis began, and he still favored invading Cuba even after the Soviets had withdrawn their missiles.[[203]](#cite_note-205) Twenty-five years later, LeMay still believed that "We could have gotten not only the missiles out of Cuba, we could have gotten the Communists out of Cuba at that time."[[126]](#cite_note-jstor2538995-126)

By 1962, President Kennedy had faced four crisis situations: the failure of the [Bay of Pigs Invasion](/wiki/Bay_of_Pigs_Invasion "Bay of Pigs Invasion");[[204]](#cite_note-206) settlement negotiations between the pro-Western government of Laos and the [Pathet Lao](/wiki/Pathet_Lao "Pathet Lao") communist movement ("Kennedy sidestepped Laos, whose rugged terrain was no battleground for American soldiers."[[205]](#cite_note-Karnow-207): 265); the construction of the [Berlin Wall](/wiki/Berlin_Wall "Berlin Wall"); and the Cuban Missile Crisis. Kennedy believed that another failure to gain control and stop communist expansion would irreparably damage US credibility. He was determined to "draw a line in the sand" and prevent a communist victory in Vietnam. He told James Reston of *[The New York Times](/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* immediately after his Vienna summit meeting with Khrushchev, "Now we have a problem making our power credible and Vietnam looks like the place."[[206]](#cite_note-208)[[207]](#cite_note-209)

Since the Supreme Court was established in 1789, 116 people have served on the Court. The length of service on the Court for the 107 non-incumbent justices ranges from [William O. Douglas](/wiki/William_O._Douglas "William O. One individual bat was recorded to have lived eight years, based on dentition.[[21]](#cite_note-21) Predators of the bat include large birds such as [red-tailed hawk](/wiki/Red-tailed_hawk "Red-tailed hawk"), [American kestrels](/wiki/American_kestrel "American kestrel"), [great horned owls](/wiki/Great_horned_owl "Great horned owl"), [barn owls](/wiki/American_barn_owl "American barn owl"), and [Mississippi kites](/wiki/Mississippi_kite "Mississippi kite").[[8]](#cite_note-Wilkins_1989-8)[[22]](#cite_note-22) Mammal predators include [Virginia opossums](/wiki/Virginia_opossum "Virginia opossum"), [striped skunks](/wiki/Striped_skunk "Striped skunk"), and [raccoons](/wiki/Raccoon "Raccoon").[[8]](#cite_note-Wilkins_1989-8) Snakes such as [eastern coachwhips](/wiki/Masticophis_flagellum_flagellum "Masticophis flagellum flagellum") and gopher snakes may also prey on them, but at a lesser extent. Certain types of beetles prey on neonate and juvenile bats that have fallen to the ground.

[White-nose syndrome](/wiki/White-nose_syndrome "White-nose syndrome") (WNS) caused by infection by the fungus *[Pseudogymnoascus destructans](/wiki/Pseudogymnoascus_destructans "Pseudogymnoascus destructans")* has increased in prevalence since 2006, mostly affecting species of bats that roost underground such as the [little brown bat](/wiki/Little_brown_bat "Little brown bat"). The fungus, now suspected to have spread from accidental transportation by human cave workers, is thought to cause frequent arousals during bat hibernation, causing an individual to use fat stores much more quickly and die of starvation before the end of winter. WNS can affect *T. brasiliensis*, but has yet to be greatly introduced to their habitat due to their preference for more arid caves. WNS has low prevalence in the subtropical and tropical regions where *T. brasiliensis* resides.[[23]](#cite_note-23)

Russia, home to over 100,000 rivers,[[1]](#cite_note-natgeo-3) is divided into [twenty watershed districts](/wiki/Watershed_district_(Russia) "Watershed district (Russia)"). It has one of the world's largest surface water resources, with its lakes containing approximately one-quarter of the world's liquid [fresh water](/wiki/Fresh_water "Fresh water").[[25]](#cite_note-30) Russia is second only to [Brazil](/wiki/Brazil "Brazil") by [total renewable water resources](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_total_renewable_water_resources "List of countries by total renewable water resources").[[26]](#cite_note-31)

Forty of Russia's rivers longer than 1,000 kilometres (620 mi) are east of the Ural Mountains, including the three major rivers that drain Siberia as they flow northward to the Arctic Ocean: the [Irtysh](/wiki/Irtysh "Irtysh")-[Ob](/wiki/Ob_River "Ob River") system (totaling 5,380 kilometres or 3,340 miles), the [Yenisey](/wiki/Yenisey "Yenisey") (5,075 kilometres or 3,153 miles), and the [Lena](/wiki/Lena_River "Lena River") (4,294 kilometres or 2,668 miles), they are among the [world's longest rivers](/wiki/World%27s_longest_rivers "World's longest rivers").[[27]](#cite_note-rivers-32) The basins of those river systems cover about eight million square kilometres (3.1 million square miles), discharging nearly 50,000 cubic meters of water per second (1.8 million cu ft/s) into the Arctic Ocean. The northward flow of these rivers means that source areas thaw before the areas downstream, creating vast swamps such as the 48,000-square-kilometre (19,000 sq mi) [Vasyugan Swamp](/wiki/Vasyugan_Swamp "Vasyugan Swamp") in the center o

The State of New York in the [2020 Census](/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census") had a population of 20,201,249 and the racial makeup was 52.5% [Non-Hispanic White](/wiki/Non-Hispanic_White "Non-Hispanic White"), 19.5% [Hispanic or Latino](/wiki/Hispanic_or_Latino "Hispanic or Latino"), 14.8% Black, 9.6% [Asian](/wiki/Asian_people "Asian people"), 0.7% [Native American](/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States"), and 0.1% [Pacific Islander](/wiki/Pacific_Islander "Pacific Islander").[[11]](#cite_note-11)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Largest_ancestry_of_each_New_York_county_%28en%29.svg/250px-Largest_ancestry_of_each_New_York_county_%28en%29.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Largest_ancestry_of_each_New_York_county_(en).svg)

New York ethnic distribution, 2000

According to 2004 estimates, 20.4% of the population was foreign-born. Among cities in the State of New York, 36% of New York City's population is foreign-born; this figure of approximately 3 million is a higher total number of foreign-born residents than any other U.S. city. This number is often around 20% in other cities across New York.

Confusingly, the term [American Jew](/wiki/American_Jews "American Jews") is used to describe [ethnic](/wiki/Ethnic_group "Ethnic group") Jews by some demographers, and religious identity (religious Jews, see: [Judaism](/wiki/Judaism "Judaism")) of various nationalities and various denominations by others. Regardless, collectively most are American-born and are a major social presence in New York. An estimated 1 to 2 million alone in New York City and another 1 to 1.5 million live in surrounding areas, sometimes New York is referred to as the "world's largest [Jewish](/wiki/Jew "Jew") city" since the mid-19th century. The season rose to the number one spot on Netflix in the first week of its release.[[14]](#cite_note-Deadline-2022-10-08-15) In the second week of its release, Netflix announced that *Dahmer* was its ninth most popular English-language TV show of all time, with 56 million households having viewed all 10 episodes.[[15]](#cite_note-16)[[16]](#cite_note-17)[[17]](#cite_note-:1-18) The season remained number-one for weeks and became Netflix's second most-viewed English Netflix season of all time, and the fourth highest across any language with 701.37 million hours viewed in 21 days.[[4]](#cite_note-:0-5) The season amassed more than 865 million hours viewed in the first 28 days of its release.[[18]](#cite_note-19) In 60 days it became the third Netflix season to pass 1 billion views.[[19]](#cite_note-20)

*Dahmer* debuted at number-one on the [Nielsen](/wiki/Nielsen_TV_ratings "Nielsen TV ratings") Top 10 streaming chart by garnering more than 3.6 billion minutes of viewing for the week of September 19–25, placing it 10th on the all-time list for single-week viewership.[[20]](#cite_note-21) The following week, it jumped to No. 7 on the all-time list with 4.4 billion minutes viewed.[[17]](#cite_note-:1-18) The season topped Nielsen's streaming chart for the third consecutive week with 2.3 billion viewing minutes.[[21]](#cite_note-22)

Jermey Dick of *[MovieWeb](/wiki/MovieWeb "MovieWeb")* stated that on "October 3rd through the 9th the views of the Dahmer season made up to 205 million hours streamed" into watching the show for that period, overall making it up to "701 million hours watched globally".[[22]](#cite_note-23)
